text: There are four cameras in this phone, in three modules.
On the back is the forty-eight megapixel Fusion main camera. Its f one point six lens lets in a lot of light, and its whole sensor shifts to cancel out the shake of your hands.
Beside it is a forty-eight megapixel ultra wide, with a hundred and twenty degree view. It can also focus close enough for macro shots. Both are the same class of camera as the standard iPhone's.
There's no separate telephoto lens. Instead, the main camera uses the middle of its sensor for a two times zoom, at twelve megapixels.
Each camera is a stack of tiny lenses, focusing light onto an image sensor.

Let's zoom into the sensor. It's covered in millions of light wells called photodiodes. Over each one sits a tiny lens and a red, green or blue filter, in a repeating pattern with twice as many greens, because our eyes are most sensitive to green.
When light hits a photodiode, it knocks electrons loose. The brighter the light, the more electrons collect. The chip counts them, pixel by pixel, and blends neighboring colors to build the image.
For selfies, there's a twelve megapixel Center Stage camera on the outer screen, in a module so thin it fits inside a five millimeter half. And on the inside, the camera under the screen.

Folding adds new tricks, too. Stand it up like a tent, and Smart Capture takes the photo when everyone's ready. Or turn on dual-screen preview, so the people in the photo can see themselves on the outer screen. Next: sound and touch.
